endorsements.quote: Acknowledge that all diagnostic and therapeutic decisions should be led by the physician's professional knowledge and clinical judgment.

The physician's duty of professional review of AI‐generated content (e.g., verifying diagnostic basis, excluding algorithmic bias) and the right of final decision signature constitute the basis of responsibility.

unlisted_practices: Embed AI literacy education modularly from early undergraduate years in medical curricula.
Assess medical students' AI literacy using a multi-modal framework of knowledge tests, situational judgment tests, and OSCEs.
Use a multi-stage longitudinal assessment of medical students' AI literacy (pre-enrollment, pre-clinical, post-clinical).
Prioritize the use of clinically validated AI tools and refrain from using experimental AI products in routine clinical practice.
Train medical students to explain the function and limitations of AI tools to patients.
Teach medical students health data governance, de-identification, and personal data protection skills.

screen.reason: Expert consensus statement and Delphi study defining core AI competencies and multi-modal assessment frameworks for medical students' AI education and literacy.
